title: Generate perf-canary baselines from controlled prod-like load runs
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes: Adds benchmark-lab baseline generator job producing versioned per-model baseline artifacts (latency + tokens/sec + attribution metrics) for perf-canary regression evaluation.
body: Summary: This PR adds a repeatable baseline generator job in benchmark-lab that computes per-model performance baseline distributions from a controlled prod-like load run. The output artifacts are written in a stable, versioned format that perf-canary can consume for regression evaluation (min samples + percent-change thresholds). Motivation: perf-canary needs a durable baseline per (model, model_version, runtime_build, hardware_sku, region) that reflects real scheduler behavior (queueing/batching) without using customer traffic. Early experiments were using ad-hoc queries on ephemeral metrics, which made it hard to reproduce baselines and triggered baseline drift/cardinality issues during rollout. This job makes baselines an explicit artifact with an audit trail and a consistent schema. Scope / What’s included: (1) New job `baselinegen` that ingests a benchmark-lab load-run result bundle (request-level summary events + runtime counters) and computes: end-to-end latency histograms (p50/p95/p99 + full histogram buckets), runtime-only latency histograms, prefill and decode latency histograms, queueing time histogram, tokens/sec distribution, batch size distribution, and optional KV cache hit-rate summary when present. (2) Baseline artifact format: a single JSON artifact per dimension key, plus an index manifest for discovery. Artifacts are content-addressed and include schema versioning so perf-canary can validate compatibility. (3) Versioning & determinism: the job pins bucket boundaries, uses a seed for any sampling, and stores the exact input run id + git sha + job config in the metadata header. (4) Output location: writes to object storage under `s3://redwood-perf-baselines/perf_canary/v1/` (prod) and `s3://redwood-perf-baselines-staging/perf_canary/v1/` (staging). Includes a thin abstraction so storage backend can be swapped later without touching canary. (5) Guardrails: hard cap on dimensions written per execution (default 200) to prevent accidental wide fanout; rejects any input that contains raw prompts or request payloads (asserts only shape metrics and aggregated counters). (6) Documentation: adds `docs/perf_canary_baselines.md` describing schema, dimension keys, and how to generate/validate a baseline for a new model or hardware SKU. Non-goals: This does not change perf-canary evaluation logic or alert thresholds (handled in perf-canary repo / ADR). This does not add customer-traffic shadowing. Implementation notes: Input contract expects a `loadrun.jsonl.zst` (one line per request summary) and `runtime_metrics.pb.zst` (aggregated runtime counters) produced by existing benchmark-lab load runner. For histograms we use fixed bucket edges aligned with existing observability-pack dashboards to avoid mismatch between baseline and live metrics. The artifact JSON is intentionally flat and explicit (no nested structures beyond a small header), to keep it easy to diff/review and to allow simple validation in the canary service. Example artifact key: `model=llama-3.1-70b-instruct|model_version=2026-01-10|runtime_build=redwood-1.42.0|kernel_set=flashattn-v3|hardware_sku=h100-sxm|region=us-east-1|tier=hosted`. Testing: Unit tests cover histogram generation, percentile extraction, bucket edge stability, manifest writing, and schema validation. Integration test runs baselinegen on a small fixture loadrun bundle and asserts stable output (golden files). Added a dry-run mode that prints the computed dimension keys and sample counts without writing artifacts. Rollout plan: (1) Run job nightly in staging for the initial canary model set (2-3 models) and compare variance vs current ad-hoc baselines. (2) After sign-off from Runtime + Telemetry, enable in prod with a manual trigger path (run-id passed explicitly) before moving to scheduled runs. (3) Wire perf-canary baseline fetch to the manifest index (separate PR already in progress in perf-canary repo). Links: Linear ENG-4874 (baseline store + versioning), ENG-4872 (perf-canary MVP), ENG-4873 (metrics definitions). Notes for reviewers: Please sanity-check the dimension key policy (especially `kernel_set` and `runtime_build`), histogram bucket edges, and the cardinality guardrails. Also confirm the artifact header contains enough info for audit/debug but not enough to leak sensitive data.
commits: benchmark-lab: add baselinegen CLI scaffolding and config parsing
baselinegen: compute latency histograms + percentiles with fixed bucket edges
baselinegen: add tokens/sec, batch size, queueing-time summary + tests
baseline artifacts: write manifest index + content-addressed artifact paths
docs: add perf_canary_baselines.md and example invocation
ci: add golden integration test for baselinegen fixture bundle
review_conversation: Rina Kobayashi: Can we guarantee that the input bundle never contains prompts? I want a hard assertion, not just 'we don't use them'.

Nadia Rahman (author): Yep — added an explicit schema check that rejects any field named prompt/input/text, and the loader only accepts the request-shape fields (prompt_tokens, max_new_tokens, observed_new_tokens) plus timing/counter fields. Added a unit test that fails on prompt-like fields.
Noah Patel: Dimension key question: do we really want `kernel_set` as a baseline dimension? It might explode variants and make baselines sparse.

Nadia Rahman (author): Agree on sparsity risk. Proposed compromise: include kernel_set in the artifact header for attribution, but only include it in the key when `--dimension-policy=debug` is enabled. Default policy keeps it out of the key. Updated config + docs accordingly.
Logan Wright: Bucket edges should match our emitted histogram buckets in metrics; otherwise dashboards/regression evaluator will mismatch. Can you link the source of truth?
Nadia Rahman (author): Bucket edges are now imported from `internal/metrics/buckets.go` (same file used by load runner aggregation). Added a test asserting bucket arrays haven’t drifted (hash).
Allison Grant: Add guardrails for how many dimension combos can be written per job run. We need a safety rail against a bad config writing thousands of artifacts.
Nadia Rahman (author): Added `--max-artifacts` (default 200) with a hard fail if exceeded, plus a dry-run summary to view dimension keys before writing.
Allison Grant: LGTM after the guardrail change.
Noah Patel: Approved. Please ensure the manifest contains sample counts per key; canary should enforce min samples.
Nadia Rahman (author): Added `sample_count` and `window_seconds` to manifest entries; canary can reject low sample baselines.
